questions: Do your eyelid drooping or difficulty keeping your eyes open worsen with sustained activity or later in the day and improve after rest?
Do you have double vision that comes and goes?
Do you have difficulty swallowing, chewing, or speaking, especially after prolonged use?
Have you had shortness of breath when lying down or after minimal activity?
Do your leg or foot weaknesses worsen with walking and improve after resting?
Do you also have weakness in your arms, neck, or face?
Do you have difficulty climbing stairs, rising from a chair, or lifting your arms overhead?
Did the eye symptoms and leg weakness begin around the same time?
Did these symptoms develop suddenly over minutes or hours?
Have the symptoms been progressively worsening over days, weeks, or months?
Do you have numbness, tingling, or reduced sensation in your feet or legs?
Do you have burning pain or electric-shock-like pain in your legs or lower back?
Have you had new difficulty controlling urination or bowel movements?
Have you had recent illness, diarrhea, surgery, vaccination, or significant infection before these symptoms began?
Do you have diabetes, thyroid disease, or another autoimmune disease?
Have you ever had similar episodes that resolved or substantially improved?
Does anyone in your family have similar weakness, foot drop, or a diagnosed neuromuscular disease?
Are you taking medicines known to cause muscle or nerve weakness, including statins, steroids, sedatives, or antibiotics such as fluoroquinolones or aminoglycosides?
Have you been exposed to alcohol, recreational drugs, pesticides, or other toxins recently?
Do you have a history of cancer, particularly lung cancer?

results: 1. Detailed neurological examination with assessment of strength, reflexes, sensation, gait, tandem walking, and cranial nerves
cranial nerve examination: bilateral abduction limitation, worse on the right, with diplopia in all directions
limb strength (MRC) examination: mild distal limb weakness
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: reduced or absent reflexes; flexor plantar responses
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): distal loss of vibration and proprioception
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
2. Examination for inconsistency and distractibility, including Hoover’s sign, hip abductor sign, ankle dorsiflexion with distraction, and variability of the foot drop
not performed / not available
3. Bedside assessment of ocular alignment and extraocular movements during sustained upgaze, repeated blinking, and distraction
sustained upgaze fatigability test: no fatigable droop
ocular motility examination: bilateral limitation of abduction, worse on the right, with diplopia in all directions
cover test / ocular alignment: orthophoric
4. Ice-pack test applied to the more ptotic eyelid
ice-pack test: negative
5. Serum acetylcholine-receptor antibodies, MuSK antibodies, and LRP4 antibodies
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative
anti-MuSK antibodies: negative
6. Repetitive nerve stimulation and single-fiber electromyography
repetitive nerve stimulation: normal
single-fibre EMG: normal jitter
7. Nerve-conduction studies and needle electromyography of both legs and representative upper-limb and facial muscles
nerve conduction studies: demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy
needle electromyography: chronic neurogenic changes
8. MRI of the brain and orbits with contrast
MRI orbits: normal extraocular muscles, no mass
MRI brain with contrast: bilateral contrast enhancement and THICKENING of cranial nerves III through XII
9. MRI of the cervical and lumbosacral spine with contrast
MRI spine: symmetrical thickening of the lumbosacral nerve roots
10. Serum creatine kinase, thyroid function tests, ANA, ESR, CRP, vitamin B12, folate, copper, and serum protein electrophoresis
thyroid function (TSH, free T4): normal
creatine kinase: normal
antinuclear antibodies and anti-dsDNA: normal
ESR / CRP: normal - against giant cell arteritis
vitamin B12 with methylmalonic acid: normal
serum folate: normal
serum copper and caeruloplasmin: normal
11. Lumbar puncture for cerebrospinal-fluid analysis
lumbar puncture / CSF: protein mildly raised at 73 mg/dL
12. Formal neuro-ophthalmology assessment with orthoptic examination and prolonged video-oculography
video-oculography / eye-movement recording: bilateral abduction deficit, worse on the right, with gaze-dependent diplopia
ocular motility examination: bilateral limitation of abduction, worse on the right, with diplopia in all directions
cover test / ocular alignment: orthophoric
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Immune-mediated chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP) with hypertrophic polyradiculopathy and extensive cranial-nerve involvement causing ophthalmoplegia

ALTERNATIVE: CANOMAD syndrome (chronic ataxic neuropathy with ophthalmoplegia, IgM paraprotein, cold agglutinins, and disialosyl antibodies)

ALTERNATIVE: Guillain–Barré syndrome, particularly the ophthalmoplegic/Miller Fisher spectrum

ALTERNATIVE: Infiltrative leptomeningeal neuropathy, such as neurolymphomatosis or neurosarcoidosis
